title: The Mood Induction Task: A standardized, computerized laboratory procedure for altering mood state in humans
protocol: Obtain informed consent from the subject prior to any procedure.
Ask the subject if they are getting a negative or positive mood induction.
For negative mood induction: ask subjects to “select the saddest piece of music”.
Play Adagio for strings, Op. 11 by Samuel Barber.
Play Adagio in G Minor by Tomaso Albinoni.
Do not name the pieces; simply ask them to select piece 1 or 2.
For positive mood induction: ask subjects to “select the happiest piece of music”.
Play Piano Concerto No. 4, Op. 58 in G Major: III. Rondo: Vivace by Ludwig van Beethoven.
Play Serenade No. 13 KV 525 G-Major: I. Serenade. Allegro by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.
Do not name the pieces; simply ask them to select piece 1 or 2.
For neutral mood induction: play The Planets, Op. 32: VII. Neptune, the Mystic by Gustav Holst.
Ensure that the subject listens to at least 1 minute of each piece of music.
Allow subjects to move onto the next piece after a minimum of 1 minute.
Enable subjects to take as much time as needed to make decisions about their mood induction.
Check that the volume of the music is comfortable for the subjects: not too quiet, not too loud.
Use ‘around-ear’ headphones so the experimenter can faintly hear the music to confirm it is playing.
Have subjects complete baseline visual analogue ratings scales by making a single vertical mark along each 10cm horizontal line.
Provide detailed instructions to the subject regarding the mood induction procedure.
Ask if the subject needs clarification and answer any questions.
Remind the subject that they can stop the experiment at any time.
Ensure that the task loads the correct piece of music.
Tell the subject that they can start the task as soon as they like.
Wait for the subject to press the spacebar or click next.
Display the first sentence on screen once the subject initiates.
Continue playing the music throughout the experiment.
Show the 'next' button after each sentence has been displayed for 12 seconds.
Use negative Velten sentences for the negative mood induction.
Use positive Velten sentences for the positive mood induction.
Use neutral Velten sentences for the neutral mood induction.
Display each sentence on screen for 12 seconds.
Ensure subjects cannot proceed before 12 seconds have elapsed.
Leave subjects alone during the task duration.
Do not enter the room to avoid distracting subjects.
Loop music back to the beginning immediately upon completion.
Have subjects make vertical lines on a second set of visual analogue rating scales while the music used in the induction continues to play.
Ensure that the music continues during this ratings-scale phase.
Measure change in mood as a change in ratings from pre-induction to post-induction.
Avoid communicating with the subject unless they request to end the experiment, in which case do so immediately.
Remain neutral and communicate minimally if intervention is necessary.
Stop the music and have the subject complete additional probes.
Repeat stage 10 rating scales and play music at suitable pause points.
Ensure the headphones are replaced if removed to complete interim tasks.
Ask the subject for feedback at the end of testing.
Provide the subject with whatever they need to feel better (e.g., allow them to watch television and/or listen to positive music).
Answer any questions the subject may have.
Do not allow the subject to leave until their mood state is back to normal.
